title: A day of local food in the Roaring Fork Valley
lede: From the valley's first homestead to a Michelin-starred dinner: a ranch walk, a farm-shop lunch, a ride up Maroon Creek, and kitchens that name the farms on your plate.
route: Carbondale → Basalt → Aspen, about 45 minutes of driving in all (Hwy 82). The evening has an up-valley and a down-valley option.

inspired.label: Roaring Fork + Farm Map
inspired.note: The valley tourism boards' guide to local food champions, farms and visitor ranches. Plan built 2026-10-04.

stops.title: Start where valley farming began
stops.why: An 1885 homestead kept with the Thompson family's own furniture and belongings. The Roaring Fork + Farm Map calls it the starting point for any farm visit.
stops.tip: Tours are by appointment only. Book through the historical society before you go.

stops.title: Walk a working regenerative ranch
stops.why: A 113-acre regenerative-agriculture and education ranch between Carbondale and Basalt, with farm tours and hayrides. Its vegetables turn up at Element 47.
stops.tip: Open Wed–Fri 9am–4pm, plus Saturday mornings in summer.

alt.why: On a Friday morning, pick your own at the Basalt farm whose vegetables supply Bosq.

stops.title: Lunch at a farmhouse kitchen

place.node: Meat & Cheese Restaurant and Farm Shop

stops.why: Aspen's farm-shop restaurant: local eggs, produce and cheese at the counter, Mesa Microgreens from Silt on the plate.
stops.tip: Hours change with the season, and it closes in November. Check before you go.

stops.title: Get out on the ranch
stops.why: A family ranch on Maroon Creek Road since 1938. Maroon Bells Outfitters runs its summer trail rides.

alt.why: Prefer to stay on foot? Visit the nonprofit farm at Cozy Point Ranch for classes, tours and the farm market.

stops.title: Dinner up valley
stops.why: Barclay Dodge's Michelin-starred kitchen, cooking with Two Roots Farm vegetables and Mesa Microgreens.

alt.why: The Little Nell's dining room publishes its full purveyor list, from Rock Bottom Ranch vegetables to Cross Creek Farms Wagyu.

stops.title: Head back down valley for the evening
stops.why: Stop for a tasting in Basalt. Nearly everything in the bottle is grown in Colorado, and its apple brandy goes into Il Porcellino's salami.

alt.why: Carbondale's distillery runs on grain grown less than a mile away by partners like Nieslanik Beef.
Seasonal dinner in Glenwood Springs, with Mesa Microgreens from just down the road.
On a summer Thursday, finish at the rodeo in Carbondale.

pantry.title: Take the valley home
pantry.why: Pick up local meat and eggs before you leave.
